properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECDH capability available in the shipped library (elliptic@6.4.0, declared in yarn.lock): no direct ECDH key-agreement call site found in src/. The application's elliptic-curve use is secp256k1 ECDSA signing/keygen via bitcoinjs-lib and ethereumjs-tx — those use sites are filed separately. Changeable here only insofar as the dependency tree is updated.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Declared dependency (yarn.lock). tweetnacl@0.14.5 ships XSalsa20-Poly1305 authenticated encryption, Ed25519 signatures and X25519 ECDH with the build; no direct call site found in src/ (it is a transitive dependency, not in package.json's direct deps). Presence is the inventory question here: the primitives ship with the installed tree.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Declared dependency (yarn.lock). elliptic@6.4.0 is the EC library (secp256k1/P-256 etc., ECDSA, ECDH, key generation) shipped in the installed tree — a transitive dependency (not in package.json's direct deps; the app's own direct EC use goes through bitcoinjs-lib/ethereumjs-*). Same package underlies the ALG-c9ffc8a8 (ECDH) object. No direct elliptic call site in src/.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Declared dependency (yarn.lock). hash.js@1.1.3 (SHA family/RIPEMD implementations) ships with the installed tree as a transitive dependency of the ethereumjs stack; no direct call site in src/ (src hashes go through Node's crypto.createHash and ethereumjs-util).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Direct dependency (package.json "pbkdf2": "^3.0.12") and actively used: src/wallet-crypto.js:5 requires it and stretchPassword/pbkdf2 (lines 313-326) call pbkdf2Sync with the SHA-1 PRF as the wallet-payload KDF; src/wallet.js:644 and src/address.js:266 also call it. This is the KDF behind the wallet's password-based encryption.
